title: Solar vs. Lunar Eclipse: Why They're Rare | Space Atlas
description: A solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse are opposite alignments of the Sun, Earth, and Moon. See why they don't happen every month with an interactive tilt model.
ogTitle: Solar vs. Lunar Eclipse: Why They're Rare
ogDescription: Toggle the Moon's real ~5° orbital tilt and see why most new moons and full moons don't produce an eclipse.
jsonldName: Solar vs. Lunar Eclipse: Why They're Rare
jsonldDescription: An interactive Sun-Earth-Moon alignment model with a toggleable orbital tilt, showing why eclipses require both syzygy and node-crossing.
